title: Brakes dragging
h1: Why are my brakes dragging or one wheel hot?
metaDesc: Brakes dragging, one wheel hot or the parking brake stuck? Answer a few questions to see if it's a caliper, the parking brake or the hydraulics, and how urgent it is.
synonyms: car feels like brakes are on
intro: A dragging brake stays partly on when you're not pressing the pedal. You may notice a hot wheel, a burning smell, the car pulling to one side, or a car that feels like it's working harder than it should. Answer a few questions to find which brake is sticking and how soon to deal with it.
safety: If you see smoke from a wheel or smell strong burning, pull over safely and let the brakes cool before going near them.
If the brake pedal goes soft or sinks, or the car is much harder to stop, stop driving and have it towed.
If the red brake warning light stays on with the parking brake fully released, have the brakes checked before driving.
Never touch a brake rotor or wheel to test it. It can be hot enough to burn you.

q_what_happens.help: A caliper is the clamp at each wheel that squeezes the brake pads against the disc (rotor).

opts.a: Smoke from a wheel, or a strong burning smell
The brake pedal feels hard or high, and all the wheels seem to drag
The parking brake won't fully release, or its warning light stays on
The car pulls to one side while driving
It started right after brake work
The car feels held back, doesn't coast well, or one wheel seems hot

q_where.q: After a short drive with little braking, hold your hand near each wheel without touching it. Which fits?
q_where.help: A 10-minute drive on quiet roads with gentle braking works best. A dragging brake gives off noticeably more heat than the others.

opts.a: One front wheel is much hotter than the other
One or both rear wheels are much hotter
They all feel about the same

q_parking.help: Most cars have either a hand lever, a foot pedal, or an electronic button (often marked with a P in a circle).

opts.a: The red brake light stays on even though the parking brake is fully released
I have a hand lever or foot pedal, and the rear still drags after releasing it
I have an electronic parking brake, and it won't release or shows a warning

result.title: A brake may be overheating, possibly from sticking on
result.now: Pull over somewhere safe, turn off the engine and let the brakes cool for at least 30 minutes. Then have the car towed or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If there are flames, get everyone away from the car and call 911.

If it happened only after a long, steep downhill with heavy braking and all the wheels were hot, the brakes may have overheated from use rather than sticking. Overheating can still damage pads, rotors and fluid, so have them checked before driving further. On long hills, use a lower gear.
If the brake pedal felt soft, sank, or the car took longer to stop, the brakes may not work normally even after cooling. Don't drive it.
If you see fluid around the inside of a wheel, tell the shop. A brake fluid leak can lead to brake failure.
result.why: Smoke or a burning smell usually means a brake is getting far hotter than normal. That often happens when it doesn't release, so it rubs constantly. Overheated brakes can fade and stop working well, and in bad cases can set grease or the tire alight.

causes.name: Sticking caliper
causes.clues: The smell and heat come from one wheel, and the car pulls toward that side.

causes.name: Parking brake left on or not releasing
causes.clues: The heat is at the rear, and the parking brake light may be on.

causes.name: Heavy braking on a long descent
causes.clues: It happened at the bottom of a steep hill, and all wheels are hot.
causes.against: If only one wheel is hot, a sticking brake is more likely.

you: Make sure the parking brake is fully released.
Once cool, look for fluid around the inside of each wheel.
shop: Pad and rotor heat damage check

result.title: A fault in the brake system may be holding all the brakes on (brake hydraulics or booster)
result.now: Don't drive it. Have the car towed or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If the brakes release after the car sits and cools, then drag again after driving, tell the shop. It can point to the master cylinder or the brake fluid.
If anyone recently added fluid, tell the shop what was used. The wrong fluid can make seals swell.
If you smell burning or see smoke from any wheel, keep everyone clear of the hot wheels and let them cool before anyone goes near them.
result.why: When every wheel drags at once, the cause is often in the parts shared by all four brakes: the master cylinder, the brake booster, or the fluid itself. Brakes that won't release can overheat quickly and then fade when you need them.

causes.name: Master cylinder not releasing pressure
causes.clues: The drag builds up as you drive and eases when the car sits.

causes.name: Brake booster or pedal not returning
causes.clues: The pedal sits higher than normal or doesn't spring back fully.

causes.name: Contaminated or wrong brake fluid
causes.clues: Recent fluid top-up from an unknown bottle, or very dark fluid.

shop: Brake booster and pedal return check

result.title: One brake may be stuck on (a sticking caliper)
result.now: A dragging brake can overheat and stop working well, so don't drive it until it's checked. Have it towed, or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If you smell burning or see smoke, stop and let it cool, then have it towed.
If the pull gets stronger, the pedal feels soft or different, or the car takes longer to stop, stop driving it and have it towed.
If the red brake warning light comes on, stop driving and have the brakes checked before going further.
result.why: Calipers slide on pins and use a piston that can corrode or stick. When one doesn't release, its pads keep rubbing. That wheel gets hot, the car pulls toward it, and the pads and rotor wear out fast. A shop will usually check the slide pins, piston and hose before deciding which part needs replacing.

causes.name: Seized or sticking caliper slide pins
causes.clues: Pads on that wheel are worn unevenly, inner versus outer.

causes.name: Sticking caliper piston
causes.clues: An older car, or a torn rubber boot around the piston.

causes.name: Collapsed brake hose acting like a one-way valve
causes.clues: The drag gets worse after each stop.

you: After a short drive, compare how much heat each wheel gives off, without touching them.
Look for brown or black brake dust heavier on one wheel.
shop: Raise the car and spin each wheel by hand
Caliper, slide pin and piston inspection

result.title: The parking brake may not be fully releasing
result.now: Make sure the lever or pedal is fully released. If the drag and any hot or burning wheel go away completely, have the rear brakes and cables checked within a few days. If it still drags, don't drive it. Have it towed or call a mechanic who comes to you.
if: If it's stuck after a cold, wet night, it may free up once the car warms. Have the cables checked anyway, since it will likely happen again.
If you smell burning or see smoke from the rear, stop and have it towed.
If the red brake light stays on after the parking brake is fully released, or the pedal feels soft, don't drive it until the brakes are checked. That can mean low brake fluid.
result.why: Parking brake cables can rust or freeze, and the springs or parts inside rear brakes can stick. When they don't fully release, the rear brakes keep rubbing, overheat and wear quickly.

causes.name: Rusted or frozen parking brake cable
causes.clues: It happens in cold or wet weather, or the lever feels stiff.

causes.name: Rear brake parts sticking or out of adjustment
causes.clues: One rear wheel is hotter, or there's a scraping noise.

causes.name: Parking brake switch out of adjustment
causes.clues: The light stays on but the wheels turn freely.

you: Check the lever or pedal goes all the way to its released position.
Compare heat from the rear wheels after a short drive, without touching them.

result.title: The electronic parking brake may not be releasing
result.now: Check the owner's manual for the release steps, which usually involve the brake pedal, the button and the engine running. If it won't release, have the car towed or call a mechanic who comes to you rather than forcing it.
if: If the battery is weak or was recently disconnected, the system may need a reset or a scan tool.
If a rear brake is hot, smells burning or is smoking, don't drive it until it's been checked.
If the pedal feels soft or the red brake light stays on once the parking brake is released, don't drive it until the brakes are checked.
result.why: An electronic parking brake uses small motors at the rear calipers. A weak battery, a failed motor or a system fault can stop it from releasing, and driving against it can damage the brakes quickly.

causes.name: Parking brake motor or caliper fault
causes.clues: A parking brake warning message and a grinding or whirring sound from one rear wheel.

causes.name: Low battery voltage
causes.clues: Slow cranking or other electrical warnings.

causes.name: System needs a reset after brake work
causes.clues: It started after the rear brakes were serviced.

you: Follow the manual's release steps exactly.
Note any message on the dash.

result.title: The red brake light with the parking brake off can mean low brake fluid
result.now: Don't drive until the brakes are checked. With the engine off, look at the brake fluid level in the reservoir, then have the car towed or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If the fluid is low, look for wet spots near the wheels or under the car. A leak can lead to brake failure.
If the fluid is full and the pedal feels normal, a parking brake switch fault is possible, but let a technician confirm it before driving.
Topping up the fluid isn't a fix. Low brake fluid with no leak you can see still needs an inspection before driving, since leaks can hide inside the wheels or under covers.
If the pedal feels soft or sinks, don't move the car.
result.why: The red brake light covers the parking brake and the brake fluid level. If it stays on with the parking brake released, fluid may be low from a leak or very worn pads, which can affect stopping.

causes.name: Low brake fluid from a leak
causes.clues: Wet spots near a wheel, or a soft pedal.

causes.name: Very worn brake pads
causes.clues: Grinding when braking, and fluid only slightly low.

causes.name: Parking brake switch stuck on
causes.clues: Fluid is full and the brakes feel normal.

you: Check the brake fluid level against the MIN and MAX marks.
Look for wet spots inside the wheels or under the car.

result.title: Something from the recent brake work may be binding
result.now: Stop driving it for now. A brake left binding after recent work can overheat and stop working well. Call the shop that did the work, tell them which wheel is hot or noisy, and ask them to come to you or arrange a tow.
if: If you smell burning or see smoke, stop and have it towed.
If the pedal feels soft or sinks, stop driving and have it towed.
If the red brake warning light comes on or the car takes longer to stop, stop driving and have it towed.
result.why: New pads that fit too tightly, slide pins that weren't cleaned and lubricated, or a parking brake that needs adjusting can all keep a brake from releasing fully. The shop that did the work will want to know, and it's often a straightforward recheck, but it shouldn't wait.

causes.name: Pads binding in the caliper bracket
causes.clues: One wheel hot, starting right after new pads.

causes.name: Slide pins dry or caliper not seated
causes.clues: Noise or pulling to one side after the job.

causes.name: Rear brakes or parking brake over-adjusted
causes.clues: The rear wheels drag after rear brake work.

you: Note which wheel is warmest after a short drive, without touching it.
shop: Recheck pad fit and slide pins
Spin each wheel by hand on a lift

result.title: No wheel stands out, so something besides a single brake may be holding the car back
result.now: Check the tire pressures, then book a check for the wheel bearings and drivetrain when convenient.
if: If you hear a hum or growl that changes when you steer, a wheel bearing is a possibility. Get it checked sooner.
If the engine revs but the car is slow to pick up speed, the transmission may be slipping.
If you notice a burning smell, smoke, or one wheel much hotter than the others, treat it as a dragging brake: pull over, let it cool, and don't drive further until it's checked.
If the brake pedal feels high, hard, soft or different, have the brakes checked before driving further.
result.why: If no wheel is hotter than the others, a single sticking brake is less likely, but the hand test is rough and can't rule it out. Low tires, a worn wheel bearing, or an engine or transmission problem can also make a car feel sluggish or coast poorly. A shop can spin each wheel on a lift to check.

causes.name: Low tire pressure
causes.clues: One or more tires look low, or the tire pressure light is on.

causes.name: Worn wheel bearing
causes.clues: A hum or growl that rises with speed.

causes.name: Engine or transmission not delivering full power
causes.clues: A check engine light, or high revs without much speed.

you: Note any noises and when they happen.
shop: Spin each wheel by hand on a lift

result.title: Have the brakes checked to find which wheel is dragging
result.now: Make sure the parking brake is fully released. If the car still feels held back, don't drive it until the brakes are checked: a dragging brake can overheat and stop working well. Have it towed, or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If you notice smoke, a strong burning smell, or the pedal feels different, stop driving and have it towed.
If the car pulls to one side or one wheel is hotter than the others, a brake may be sticking. Don't drive it until it's checked.
If the red brake warning light comes on, have the brakes checked before driving further.
result.why: A shop can lift the car and spin each wheel by hand to find one that doesn't turn freely. That quickly shows whether a caliper, the parking brake or something else is causing the drag.

causes.name: Sticking caliper
causes.clues: One wheel hotter or dustier, or pulling to one side.

causes.name: Parking brake not releasing
causes.clues: Drag from the rear, especially in cold or wet weather.

causes.name: Something other than the brakes
causes.clues: Low tires or a humming wheel bearing.

you: Check the parking brake is fully released.
Look for one wheel with much more brake dust than the others.
shop: Spin each wheel by hand on a lift
